source.excerpt: Let not sleep, says Pythagoras, fall upon thy eyes till thou hast thrice reviewed the transactions of the past day.
trail: The Rambler no. 8 prints this English sentence with the interruption “says Pythagoras.” Wikiquote identifies Johnson’s translation; Stanford explains that the Golden Verses are a later compilation circulating under Pythagoras’s name. Removing the reporting phrase yields the popular sentence, not an autograph saying. Johnson’s Rambler ↗

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: Samuel Johnson’s Rambler reproduces this nightly self-examination advice in English under Pythagoras’s name. The older Golden Verses tradition is associated with Pythagorean teaching, but Johnson’s inspected eighteenth-century prose should not be passed off as an English original from antiquity.
